clue.text: Clergyman born in Lincoln?

indicators.note: in says the letter for born sits inside the president's short name

parts.note: Abraham Lincoln, US president, known as Abe; the question mark flags a name as example

explanation.surface: A churchman who happens to come from the cathedral city of Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln looks like the English city, but it is the president, Abe.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbé is a French title for a cleric, especially an abbot or priest.

clue.text: Look for extraordinary act in one's meeting with head

indicators.note: meeting with says the head comes next in line after the jumble
something extraordinary is out of the usual order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: one gives I, the Roman numeral
pate is an old word for the head

explanation.surface: Someone expecting a strange stunt when meeting the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraordinary' rearranges ACTINI into ANTICI; 'extraordinary act' looks like ANTIC, which nearly works but leaves 'in' unexplained.
explanation.definitionFit: To anticipate is to expect or look forward to something, i.e. to look for it.

clue.text: Literary sketcher protects grandma with a source of wealth

indicators.note: protects means wraps around, holding the grandmother inside

parts.note: Boz was the pen name of Dickens in Sketches by Boz
nan is a grandmother

explanation.surface: A writer looks after his grandmother, who is a rich source of money.
explanation.walkthrough: Sketches by Boz was an early Dickens book.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonanza is a rich vein of ore, and so any sudden rich source of profit.

clue.text: Unwell feeling queen needs freedom from worry

parts.note: being free of worry is being at ease, a state of easiness

explanation.surface: A monarch, feeling ill, just wants to stop worrying.
explanation.definitionFit: Queasiness is nausea, the sick sensation in the stomach of someone feeling unwell.

clue.text: Clean casks English agriculturist secured — but a few tons get lost

indicators.note: T is the abbreviation for ton; a few of them, three, are dropped

parts.note: tuns are large casks
Jethro Tull was an English agriculturist who invented the seed drill
tied means secured

explanation.surface: A farmer packs pristine barrels, though some weight goes missing.
explanation.walkthrough: One T is lost from each of the three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsullied means not dirtied or stained, pure and spotless.

clue.text: Neighbourhood introduces new sporting venue

indicators.note: introduces says the district takes the letter for new into itself

parts.note: an area is a neighbourhood

explanation.surface: A local district opens a new sports ground.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is an enclosed space or stadium for sport or spectacle.

clue.text: Banking aircraft generates a form of lift

definitions.meaning: a plane that is tilted, as when it turns, is leaning to one side
a sloping ramp is a simple machine for raising heavy loads

explanation.surface: A plane turning on its side creates a type of aerodynamic lift.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramp is one of the classic simple machines, used to raise weights with less effort.

clue.text: Cost of swans kept in river

indicators.note: kept in says the swans sit inside the river's name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
pens are female swans

explanation.surface: What it costs to keep swans on the river.
explanation.definitionFit: An expense is a cost, money paid out for something.

clue.text: Colour seen in small botanic garden

parts.note: Kew Gardens in London is the Royal Botanic Gardens

explanation.surface: A hue spotted in a little botanical garden.
explanation.definitionFit: To colour a report is to bias or distort it, which is to skew it.

clue.text: Ringing the changes for Stedman Doubles

indicators.note: in bell-ringing, ringing the changes means sounding the bells in a varying order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bell-ringers performing Stedman Doubles, a named change-ringing method.
explanation.walkthrough: Stedman Doubles is a bell-ringing method on five bells; 'Doubles' looks like part of its name but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tandem is a bicycle built for two riders, so tandems are doubles in the sense of two-seaters.

clue.text: Wildly run in a free style? That's good for cold

parts.note: in cricket an extra is a run not scored off the bat

indicators.note: G for good replaces C for cold

parts.note: vacant means free or unoccupied, so vacantly is in a free manner

explanation.surface: A runner sprinting about with abandon, and it helps when chilly.
explanation.definitionFit: Extravagantly means without restraint or beyond reasonable limits, much as wildly does.

clue.text: South Kent prison initially reported a fugitive

indicators.note: reported means the picked letters are spoken out one by one, and that run of sounds gives the word
initially takes the opening letter of each of the three words before it

parts.note: the opening letters of these three words are S, K and P

explanation.surface: News of a convict on the run from a jail in southern Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Say the letters S, K, P aloud: ess-kay-pee.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has broken out of custody and is on the run is a fugitive.

clue.text: Perhaps sign over one's property sent mistakenly during meal

indicators.note: during says the rearranged letters go inside the word for a meal

parts.note: a collation is a light meal

indicators.note: sent in the wrong order, so these four letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A property owner's sign, wrongly delivered while they were eating.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: a star sign such as Leo is a group of stars hanging in the sky over anyone's home. 'mistakenly' rearranges the four letters into NSTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Zodiac signs are named after star groupings, so a sign seen overhead is perhaps one of those patterns of stars.

clue.text: A short display of anger over ballet's dominating influence

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first pieces sit above the next
short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: making a scene is an angry public outburst
ballet is a form of dance

explanation.surface: A brief tantrum during a ballet that comes to dominate.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascendance is the position of power or control over others, a dominating sway.

clue.text: Scheme to destroy each unfinished city square

indicators.note: each of the two words loses its final letter

parts.note: a plan is a scheme
to zap something is to destroy it

explanation.surface: A plan to demolish a half-built public square in a city.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaza is an open public square in a town, from the Spanish word for place.

clue.text: Without children, girl in the Hebrides perhaps adopts son

indicators.note: in says the girl's name sits inside the islands-plus-son letters
adopts says the islands take the letter for son into themselves

parts.note: the Hebrides are Scottish islands, an example of isles
Sue is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A childless girl living in the Scottish islands takes in a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopts' and 'in' are both container signals: the son is taken into the islands first, then the girl goes in near the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue means offspring, so being issueless is having no offspring at all.

clue.text: Religious assembly heard offence with excited eagerness

indicators.note: heard says the words are spoken, giving a word spelt differently

parts.note: a sin is an offence, and agog means in excited eagerness; together they are said as sin-a-gog

explanation.surface: Someone hears, keenly and excitedly, of an offence.
explanation.definitionFit: A synagogue is a Jewish congregation as well as its building; the word comes from Greek for assembly.

clue.text: Agreed, ant may be crawling around in this restaurant?

indicators.note: an ant crawling around moves this way and that, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Diners agree an ant could be wandering about this outdoor eatery.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea garden is an outdoor café or garden where tea and refreshments are served.

clue.text: Most self-disciplined detectives in US agency turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up reads the letters from bottom to top
in says the detectives go inside the agency's letters

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency
tecs is slang for detectives

explanation.surface: Detectives working for an American agency turn out to be extremely disciplined.
explanation.walkthrough: TECS in CIA gives CITECSA, read upward. The definition is a noun: one of the most self-disciplined.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascetic practises severe self-denial, among the strictest of self-disciplined people.

clue.text: Forms of insects regularly choosing plum and plane

indicators.note: regularly choosing takes every other letter, starting from the first, of each word

explanation.surface: Insects picking evenly between plum and plane trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupae are the dormant stage between larva and adult in insects like butterflies.

clue.text: Perhaps hamper girl hemmed in by pillar

indicators.note: hemmed in by says the girl sits inside the pillar

parts.note: a pier is a pillar supporting a bridge or arch
Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Maybe a girl is held back, trapped by a pillar.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamper looks like a verb in the surface; here it is the basket.
explanation.definitionFit: A pannier is a basket carried by a horse or bicycle, a kind of hamper.

clue.text: Coriander and sage blended would be gross

indicators.note: blended herbs are mixed up together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two herbs mixed together would taste revolting.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse-grained can mean crude or vulgar, a sense shared with gross behaviour or humour.

clue.text: European paired up visiting bridge opponents

indicators.note: visiting says the married couple go inside the two bridge players

parts.note: in bridge South and East are on opposing sides
to be paired up in marriage is to be wed

explanation.surface: A European couple visiting the opposing side at a bridge table.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swede is a native of Sweden, a European country.

clue.text: Succeeded in black form of humour

indicators.note: in says the letter goes inside the word for black

parts.note: jet is a deep glossy black

explanation.surface: Black comedy that worked.
explanation.definitionFit: A jest is a joke, a light-hearted piece of humour.

clue.text: Add label to part of seat-belt — it needs reversing

indicators.note: reversing says the hidden letters are read backwards
part of says the letters lie within the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A seat-belt part needs labelling before it is turned round.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'part' into the definition; 'part of' is the indicator for the hidden letters, leaving 'Add label to' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To entitle a book or piece is to give it a title, which is adding a label.

clue.text: Nan's taken round city area, one with a certain style of architecture

definitions.text: with a certain style of architecture

indicators.note: taken round says the grandmother's letters go round the others

parts.note: nan is a grandmother, a gran
EC is the postcode for the City of London
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Grandma has been shown round a city district by an architecture buff.
explanation.definitionFit: Grecian describes buildings in the classical style of ancient Greece, with columns and pediments.

clue.text: A time saver for surveyors — they cart me around

indicators.note: around says these letters are moved round into a new order

explanation.surface: Surveyors' gadget so useful they lug it about with them.
explanation.definitionFit: A surveying instrument for fixing distances and bearings quickly, so it saves the surveyor time.

clue.text: Fish caught off Dorset castle

indicators.note: off says the letter for caught is taken away

parts.note: Corfe Castle is a ruined castle in Dorset, a county in southern England
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An angler lands something near a castle on the Dorset coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The orfe is a freshwater fish of the carp family, also called the ide.
